event: Sidy Cissoko driving dunk blocked by Steven Adams
purpose: Exact visual-state mapping for the first static free-view reconstruction proof
rationale: audio synchronization is used only as the coarse alignment layer
per-feed frame offsets are selected from the common 3D ball trajectory and visual hand/ball contact state

initial deflection is preferred over the fully occluded contact instant because the basketball is already moving outbound but remains essentially at the Adams/Cissoko hand interaction, giving a dramatic and more reconstructable single-ball state
the immediately preceding and following synchronized states are retained as explicit QA neighbors rather than discarded

evidence.ball_trajectory: The synchronized frame relationship produces a smooth physically plausible reconstructed ball path from approximately rim height downward/outward after the block.
evidence.camera_motion_compensation: Rigid basket/background geometry is tracked through the candidate frame window so pan/tilt/zoom does not masquerade as feed latency.
evidence.left_slash_manual_state: Adjacent-frame inspection previously identified Left Slash F26 as contact/start-separation and F27 as beginning deflection; the multi-view geometry independently places F27 in the selected initial-deflection state.
evidence.semantic_check: Selected frames show Cissoko still extended at the rim, Adams' blocking arm at the ball interaction, and a single distinguishable ball beginning its outbound path.

do_not_assume: Do not replace this mapping with one global frame index across all feeds.
Do not use raw audio alignment as exact visual synchrony.
Do not change the freeze state merely to make a renderer easier unless the alternate state passes the same multi-view semantic/geometry QA.
